To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the hydrogen production rate from glucose was significantly lower than that from arabinose, and that hydrogen partial pressure and pH affected hydrogen production.
the use of extreme thermophilic cultures, pH 7 and low partial hydrogen pressure, is beneficial for efficient conversion of sugars to hydrogen.

(i) arabinose and hexoses can be used as substrates for hydrogen production at extreme thermophilic conditions; (ii) hydrogen partial pressure has to be kept low to maximize hydrogen production from glucose; (iii) pH has an important effect on hydrogen production from both glucose and arabinose.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of hydrogen from arabinose in a thermophilic, continuous process, with the use of a mixed culture.
the production of hydrogen from pentoses and hexoses by extreme thermophillic anaerobic cultures, using continuous and batch processes.
the development of efficient hydrogen production technologies from lignocellulosic material, which is a major challenge in the field of biohydrogen production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hydrogen yield from arabinose is higher than from glucose.
hydrogen production from glucose was not as efficient as from arabinose, and that the effect of pH on hydrogen production from arabinoses was not as significant as from hexoses.
the use of arabinose as substrate for hydrogen production is advantageous over glucose, but only at high OLR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hydrogen production from glucose was limited by hydrogen partial pressure, whereas arabinose was not.
the hydrogen yield and production rate from arabino-oligosaccharides were higher than from glucose.

the extreme thermophilic mixed culture is a promising bioprocess for the production of hydrogen from pentoses and hexoses, and that hydrogen production rate is higher with arabinose than with glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the extreme thermophilic hydrogen fermentation of arabinose, the hydrogen production rate is higher and the hydrogen yield is higher when the hydrogen partial pressure is kept low and when pH 7 is used instead of pH5.5.
, in the case of extreme thermophilic mixed cultures, the use of pentoses as substrates for hydrogen production can be more efficient than the use of glucose.
hydrogen fermentation of sugars from lignocellulosic biomass is possible with extreme thermophilic microorganisms, and the process can be improved by using pH 7 and low hydrogen partial pressure.
